confidence_notes.canon: The in-game element exists and is documented by the game wikis or Rockstar itself. For theories it would mean Rockstar confirmed it.
confidence_notes.strong: Reported by several independent sources or press, not yet checked first-hand or confirmed by Rockstar.
confidence_notes.speculative: Fan reading, single source, or unverified report.
confidence_notes.debunked: Shown to be false, a hoax, or satire.

items.title: The 2D, 3D and HD universes
items.summary: Rockstar splits GTA into separate continuities by graphical era: 2D (GTA 1, London, GTA 2), 3D (GTA III to Vice City Stories) and HD (GTA IV onward, including GTA VI). Rockstar said the universes are the worlds 'interpreted at different definitions'. Brands, radio and background characters may recur across universes; main characters do not.

items.title: Vice City exists three times
items.summary: Vice City appears as a 2D city in GTA 1, the 1980s 3D city of Vice City and Vice City Stories, and the modern HD city in the state of Leonida in GTA VI. Same name and Miami inspiration, different continuities.

items.title: Liberty City across three universes
items.summary: Rockstar's New York stand-in exists in all three universes. In the HD universe it is the GTA IV city, referenced constantly in GTA V (Broker clothing, Liberty City licence plates, marathon chatter) and again in GTA VI (Liberty City Swingers card, a Liberty City memoir).

items.title: Lazlow Jones, the radio voice of every era
items.summary: Real-life writer and radio host Lazlow Jones voiced a fictional version of himself on GTA radio from GTA III to GTA V and appears in person in GTA V and GTA Online After Hours. The universe rule's best-known exception: a radio personality who carries across universes.
